summary: A party leader must decide whether to deliver a legislative victory to a president facing reelection from the other party.
realLife: Dirksen weighed Republican divisions and his party’s civil rights history while Johnson sought passage in 1964.
gates: The president needs opposition votes during a presidential campaign.
inGame: needs: a party leader's negotiating position tied to caucus divisions and an approaching election.

turns.what: The leader supports bringing the bill up while leaving the final vote open.
turns.pulledBy: The caucus agrees on debate but remains divided over the negotiated text.
turns.writesBack: The procedural commitment and the position on passage are recorded separately.

turns.what: The leader announces a position after members have read the substitute.
turns.pulledBy: Members object to committing on a draft they have yet to see.
turns.writesBack: The announcement refers to the circulated version.
